subject: Clarifying DPA: controller vs processor, subprocessors, and breach timing
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@navigator.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & next steps from discovery — DPA questions

Hi Tara — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups we promised to capture after the call: 

1) Roles: Based on how you described ingestion and control of patient records, you are expecting Navigator Health to be the Controller and Redwood to act as Processor. Please confirm.
2) Subprocessors: you asked for a current subprocessors list and an approval flow. I attached our latest list (redwood-subprocessors-2026-07.pdf) and a short note on our subcontractor onboarding.
3) Retention: you mentioned a 90-day retention window for derived embeddings and logs — is that a hard requirement or a preferred setting?
4) Breach notice: Navigator asked about an initial notification within 24 hours for incidents involving PHI. We typically provide an initial acknowledgement within 48 hours and a follow-up investigatory report within 30 days; see proposed options below.
5) Logging & visibility: Karhtik will follow up with the specifics on admin/audit logs and what we surface in hosted vs. private deployments.

Next steps proposed:
- Karhtik to send a short technical write-up of logging, retention, and region controls (today).
- Neha to provide the formal DPA language we typically sign and options for shorter breach-notice timelines tied to support tiers (today).
- If the above looks good, I can circulate the DPA through DocuSign and we can align on signature + pilot dates.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2026-07.pdf; redwood-dpa-summary-annotated.docx

Thanks — and let me know if I mis-captured anything.

Best,
David
David Kim | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Tara Singh <tara@navigator.health>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from discovery — DPA questions

David, thanks for the summary — that matches our notes. A few clarifying asks from Legal/Privacy here before we loop procurement: 

- Controller/Processor: yes, Navigator will be Controller. We need a clause confirming Redwood acts only as Processor and will process PHI on our instructions.
- Subprocessors: provide both (a) a current list of subprocessors and (b) confirmation you will provide 30-days notice before adding any subprocessors that will process PHI.
- Retention: 90 days for derived artifacts (embeddings, model outputs) is our baseline. Logs that contain unredacted PII must be deleted within 30 days unless a retention justification is provided.
- Breach notice: we require an initial notification within 24 hours for confirmed incidents affecting PHI and a root-cause + remediation plan within 21 days. Is that acceptable?
- Data residency: production data must remain in US regions only. Any backups should also be US-hosted.

Also: do you have an SOC 2 report or ISO attestation we can share with legal?

If you can send written answers to the above, we’ll prepare a redline. Attachments: our redline intake template (not attached here).

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Singh | Head of Security & Privacy | Navigator Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@navigator.health>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from discovery — DPA questions

Tara — quick technical answers to the items you raised (feel free to loop me in for a short screenshare):

- Controller/Processor: operationally, Redwood does not make independent decisions about data use for Navigator accounts; you can configure the account to discard raw payloads. We’ll capture the contractual language but the runtime is designed to treat customer data as customer-controlled.

- Subprocessors: attached is the latest subprocessors list (redwood-subprocessors-2026-07.pdf). For PHI-sensitive subprocessors, we can offer customer notification windows and, in some cases, an approval gating step for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Retention: 
  * Hosted (Redwood API): default ephemeral request logs kept 90 days; admin/audit logs available and can be configured for 30/90/365 day retention. Logs that contain unredacted PII can be restricted by role and purged on request — we’ll add a documented runbook for that flow.
  * Dedicated/Private: you can opt to manage persistence; we support disabling persistent KV cache and setting retention to 0 days for raw payloads.

- Logging & visibility: we export structured audit events (request_id, timestamp, user_account_id, route, model_version, token_counts). We do not persist plaintext model-internal caches when using customer-managed encryption keys (CMK).

- Breach timing: the platform can generate an initial anomaly alert quickly, but a confirmed incident timeline depends on triage. From an engineering perspective we can provide an initial notice within 24 hours for high-severity confirmed incidents if we move to an elevated support SLA (Dedicated or Enterprise support add-on).

I’m attaching a short ops note that maps retention and log controls to hosting options (privacy-ops-notes-20260804.txt). Happy to go into more detail.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@navigator.health>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from discovery — DPA questions

Tara, David — following up with the formal contract-oriented positions and options. Quoted below are our standard positions and what we can offer as exceptions for Navigator Health.

1) Controller / Processor: Redwood will sign the DPA with language that identifies Navigator Health as Controller and Redwood Inference as Processor. We will not assert joint-controllership for the processing in question.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood maintains an up-to-date list of subprocessors and publishes it before each billing cycle. Our standard commitment is to provide 30-days notice before onboarding new subprocessors. For subprocessors that will touch PHI, we can offer a customer review window and an opt-out/right-to-discontinue clause for Dedicated/Private contracts. See attached subprocessors list.

3) Retention & Logs: Standard offering — 90-day retention for request logs and derived artifacts. For unredacted logs that contain PHI we can provide a 30-day purge option by default, or retain longer by explicit written justification. Dedicated/Private customers can set retention to 0 for raw payloads. We will document the purge request runbook and the data deletion verification steps (can provide an attestation).

4) Breach notification: Our default response cadence is: initial acknowledgement within 48 hours of confirmed incident detection and a substantive incident report within 30 days. As Karthik noted, we can agree to an initial notification within 24 hours if Navigator signs up for the Enterprise support SLA (or a Dedicated capacity contract with the advanced incident response add-on). If 24 hours is required contractually without the SLA, we will need to scope additional monitoring and dedicated on-call resources and reflect that in pricing.

5) Data residency: We can pin accounts to US-only regions (production and backups) when requested; this is a high-priority deployment option for customers handling regulated data.

6) Evidence & attestation: We will share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. We can also provide copies of penetration test summaries and the privacy-op notes attachment.

Next actions I propose:
- David: propose a short call (30 minutes) with your legal and ours to align on the breach-notice window and subprocessors approval flow.
- Tara: if your legal can share a redline, we’ll mark up the DPA and return within 3 business days.

I’ve attached the DPA summary and the subprocessors list for legal review. If you want a faster 24-hour initial notice without moving to Enterprise SLA right now, we can provide a scoped statement of work and price for the additional monitoring.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor | Head, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dpa-summary-annotated.docx; redwood-subprocessors-2026-07.pdf
